description:
📝 Notes
Jan 22, 2026
R&D daily sprint
Invited Amir Houieh Unbody io Noémi Biró Gabor Kerekes
Attachments R&D daily sprint 
Meeting records Transcript 
Summary
Noémi Biró and Amir Houieh shared frustrations regarding the Carefinder project's launch issues, which were attributed to the CEO constantly adding features before sharing, and Noémi Biró also expressed concern about the safety of CTO Hussain due to intermittent internet access. Amir Houieh detailed the intense human rights situation and ongoing protests in Iran, emphasizing that international aid is necessary to achieve their goals, while Gabor Kerekes shared his experience joining a local Iranian protest. The team reviewed merged pull requests from Amir Houieh and Gabor Kerekes, planned a dedicated workshop after the sprint meeting to finalize the manifesto draft, and scheduled a discussion for Monday between Amir Houieh and Gabor Kerekes to determine hiring needs and strategy using Upwork.
Details
Personal Check-in and Workout Discussion Noémi Biró greeted the team and mentioned that they were not working from home, typically going to a location after a workout. Amir Houieh expressed an interest in working out but noted that it does not work for them, while Noémi Biró shared that having a personal trainer compels them to attend sessions. Amir Houieh also shared that they had an expensive gym subscription last year to motivate themself to go, but the financial motivation did not work (00:00:00).
Carefinder Project Issues Amir Houieh discussed frustrations with the Carefinder project, describing their current process as the "opposite of launching a product," citing issues like testing on the launch day and testing obvious features such as search accuracy. Amir Houieh attributed these issues to the team having launched three products in the last two months and the CEO acting as the only user, constantly adding features in pursuit of an "ultimate version" before sharing it. Noémi Biró emphasized the importance of avoiding similar pitfalls (00:03:54).
Concern for Hussain's Safety Noémi Biró asked about the reachability and safety of the CTO, Hussain. Amir Houieh reported limited contact with Hussain, noting that internet access in their area is intermittent, available only for a couple of minutes every few days. Amir Houieh confirmed that based on what they heard, everyone they know is currently safe, but acknowledged concern about what might happen next, mentioning the start of arrests (00:05:26).
Human Rights Situation and Protests in Iran Amir Houieh described the intense and deeply disturbing situation regarding human rights and government actions in Iran, including the collection of bodies in ceilers without records due to the large number of casualties. They shared accounts of parents having to personally identify the bodies of their loved ones and shared a distressing incident where a person was found alive after being presumed dead (00:06:46). Amir Houieh recounted a story of the killing of three protesters and the apartment owner who sheltered them by militias brought in from other countries, confirming the protests were met with lethal force (00:08:18).
Local Iranian Community and Cultural Spirit Gabor Kerekes mentioned joining an Iranian protest over the weekend and the existence of a local Iranian community, sharing an experience of meeting an Iranian café worker who had moved there in 2019 and made an effort to learn the local language (00:08:18). Amir Houieh noted that Iranians are generally inclined towards "doing parties and stuff" and shared an anecdote from a protest in Toronto where demonstrators clapped and danced for a wedding party they encountered, highlighting the cultural resilience (00:09:32). Amir Houieh emphasized that there is no way going back from the current situation and thanked Gabor Kerekes and Noémi Biró for their support (00:11:04).
Protest Strategy and International Support Amir Houieh stated that the protesters cannot achieve their goals without international help, clarifying that only sanctions will not be sufficient. They explained that the two options are either to do nothing and allow the regime to continue killing its own people at a "crazy level" or for foreign aid to come in and attack the regime's bases (00:12:22). Gabor Kerekes questioned the strategy behind the protests, given the known risk of severe government response (00:14:01). Amir Houieh explained that previous protests, where 1,500 people were killed, established the cost, but factors such as a large portion of the population living under the poverty line, political suppression, limited travel, and severe women's rights suppression created accumulated frustrations (00:15:33).
Regime Power and Catalyst for Protests Amir Houieh discussed how the opposition, led by the son of the previous king, united various groups and began showing up as a formidable opponent to the regime. They noted that a 12-day attack by Israel weakened the "powerful holy image" of the regime in the minds of many Iranians, showing that the regime was much weaker than expected and breaking the idea that "No one dares to touch them" (00:17:03). Amir Houieh stated that the life of Iranians is now different, and they cannot think the same way as they did two weeks ago (00:18:07).
Global Implications of the Iranian Regime Amir Houieh argued that the Iranian regime is a global issue, citing that the regime is the main supplier of drones for Russia against Ukraine and contributes to destabilization across the region (00:20:44). They noted that for decades the regime encouraged non-agreeing people to leave the country, which is now working against them as those who left have formed strong lobbies in the tech and political sectors. Amir Houieh added that the regime values "ideology and loyalty more than expertise," contributing to their overall weakness (00:21:52).
Project Updates and Task Review The meeting shifted to project updates, with Gabor Kerekes asking about the agenda and the team agreeing to a quick update, including reviewing time spent on tasks (00:24:21). Gabor Kerekes confirmed that cleaning on the comet was done and merged, and a pull request from Amir Houieh regarding customer io was also merged. Amir Houieh committed to reviewing the updated C Bill proposal from Melissa the following day and potentially including Noémi Biró in the review (00:25:28).
Pinterest Board Collaboration Amir Houieh shared that they invited Gabor Kerekes to a Pinterest board for lab website inspiration, emphasizing that the website should be simple. Gabor Kerekes pointed out that the board was not collaborative, needing permission changes for the team to add pins (00:26:40). Noémi Biró had difficulty accessing the board, but Gabor Kerekes helped them find the invitation under their profile's boards section (00:29:49).
Manifesto Drafting and Planning Gabor Kerekes shared that they were fixing a bug in C Bill related to creating a new conversation thread when logging in from a new browser and had written notes to brainstorm for the manifesto (00:32:25). The team agreed to schedule a dedicated workshop session, ideally right after the sprint meeting tomorrow, to finalize the first draft of the manifesto (00:34:07).
In-Person Work Planning Noémi Biró announced that they would be in the same city the following week, suggesting the possibility of in-person sessions, which Amir Houieh also expressed interest in (00:35:07). Amir Houieh offered a downstairs room at their place for Gabor Kerekes and Noémi Biró to stay (00:36:35). Both Gabor Kerekes and Noémi Biró confirmed they would plan their arrival dates for the following week, with Noémi Biró planning to stay with friends but open to in-person sessions (00:37:53).
Reviewing the C Bill Proposal Noémi Biró provided an update that their account was working and they were organizing better, and confirmed they would get in touch with Melissa after reviewing the new proposal (00:37:53). Amir Houieh sent the "drastically simplified" new proposal to the team (00:39:05).
Technical Talk and Hiring Discussion Amir Houieh stressed the need for a technical discussion with Gabor Kerekes to determine what type of help is needed for the upcoming weeks of the project, suggesting they should start hiring now (00:39:05). Amir Houieh proposed using Upwork as the most efficient way to find candidates due to the ability to see a person's entire work history and find talent at a reasonable price, and they scheduled the discussion for Monday (00:41:17).
Meeting Schedule Confirmation Noémi Biró inquired about keeping the weekly meetings with Melissa on Fridays. Amir Houieh suggested that the first meeting with Melissa would be next Friday, but proposed an additional meeting with Noémi Biró and Melissa on Monday to go over the final proposal and discuss the project start (00:42:32). Noémi Biró and Amir Houieh then worked through the process of Noémi Biró adding Amir Houieh's calendar to better coordinate scheduling (00:43:29). The final plan was confirmed: daily meeting tomorrow, followed by the manifesto workshop, and Noémi Biró would reach out to Melissa to schedule the Monday meeting .
Suggested next steps
Amir Houieh will review Melissa's changes to the C bill proposal and share the Google Docs link in the civil chat tomorrow.
Amir Houieh will fix the Cibil task today or tomorrow.
Gabor Kerekes will let Amir Houieh know the dates of their visit to Amsterdam so Amir Houieh can sync with their partner.
Noémi Biró will reach out to Melissa about scheduling a meeting to walk through the final proposal and discuss how and where to start the project.
Gabor Kerekes will finish up fixing the bug issue when opening Cibil with an account in a browser that hasn't been used before.
Gabor Kerekes, Amir Houieh, and Noémi Biró will have a workshop session tomorrow right after the sprint meeting to write the first draft of the manifesto.
Gabor Kerekes and Amir Houieh will have a technical talk on Monday to discuss the project's help needs and potential hiring, and Amir Houieh will send a meeting link for the talk.
